peralta-fremont-saddle.note: Heat safety advisory: this is an exposed, sun-elevated desert trail in the Superstition Wilderness. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for rural Maricopa and northern Pinal counties, including the Superstition Mountains and Apache Junction area, has been extended and is now in effect through August 9, 2026 at 8pm with afternoon temperatures of 106 to 118 degrees. Tonto National Forest lifted Stage 2 fire restrictions forest-wide on July 20, 2026, so there is no fire closure here currently. Hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service; Tonto National Forest.

flatiron-siphon-draw.note: Heat safety advisory: this is an exposed, sun-elevated desert trail with a history of heat-related rescues. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for rural Maricopa and northern Pinal counties, including the Superstition Mountains and Apache Junction area, has been extended and is now in effect through August 9, 2026 at 8pm with afternoon temperatures of 106 to 118 degrees. This trail is inside Lost Dutchman State Park, which has Stage II fire restrictions in effect through October 31, 2026: no wood, charcoal, or open flame, and no smoking on trails. Hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service; Arizona State Parks.

white-tank-waterfall.note: Main Trailhead Staging Area closed for construction through 9/30/26. lava-river-cave.note: FR 171, the access road from FR 245 to the Lava River Cave trailhead, remains closed to motorized vehicles for maintenance (closed since July 13, 2026); reaching the cave requires hiking or biking a longer unpaved approach. Source: Coconino National Forest (Forest Order 03-04-08-26-02).

fossil-springs.note: Heat safety advisory: this trail descends into a canyon. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for northern Gila County (below 4000 feet) expired August 3, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 6, 2026 morning check, though canyon conditions remain hot. A permit is required to park in the Fossil Creek permit area through October 1, 2026, and permits are available seven days a week for the rest of the season. Hike early morning and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service Flagstaff; Coconino National Forest.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. South Kaibab Trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source, and several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer. The National Weather Service also has an Extreme Heat Warning active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet through August 7, 2026 at 8pm, with highs of 102 to 114 degrees depending on elevation. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. Several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer, including on Bright Angel Trail. The National Weather Service also has an Extreme Heat Warning active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet through August 7, 2026 at 8pm, with highs of 102 to 114 degrees depending on elevation. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The North Rim reopened for the 2026 season on May 15 and North Kaibab Trail from the trailhead through Phantom Ranch is open to foot traffic, but the National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and Coconino Overlook due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and falling trees. No potable water is available anywhere on the North Rim, including the trailhead and Supai Tunnel; hikers must carry all water needed for the entire hike. The National Weather Service also has an Extreme Heat Warning active for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet through August 7, 2026 at 8pm; Grand Canyon National Park is urging hikers to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm due to dangerously hot conditions after several heat-related deaths this summer. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park (North Rim status update, July 31, 2026); National Weather Service Flagstaff.
